approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves fresh molecular graphs from its accepted-score population and allocates evaluations with correlated function draws from an accepted-only count-fingerprint GP. It fits a monotone unit-linear, three-tanh response transformation by Jacobian-adjusted likelihood, inverts the original latent draws into score units, and uses the transformed law's quadrature expectation to restrict stalled batches to forty candidates. The same implementation already computes an original raw-GP reference on the identical accepted archive. Its complete predictive-loss advantage coexists with lower final best scores.
approach.novelty: Replace only the location of each warped function draw with that candidate's existing raw-GP mean. Keep the learned centered residual law and the Parent's warped-mean eligibility ranking. This separates location inside sampled maxima from the eligibility consumer: the earlier raw-gate experiment changed the gate alone, and the earlier native-quantile location experiment used a different model and changed its gate too. The present experiment tests whether this isolated location substitution changes paid allocation enough to improve the complete endpoint panel.

hypothesis: A deterministic location-consumer variant of m-000000000005 on the exact unit-linear host. For candidate q and original function row j let W(q,j) be the original inverse-warped score draw, mW(q) its original 128-point quadrature expectation, and mG(q) the existing passive raw-GP posterior mean on the same chronological accepted archive. Define delta(q)=mG(q)-mW(q), active draw A(q,j)=W(q,j)+delta(q), active marginal quantile QA(q,tau)=QW(q,tau)+delta(q), active median medianW(q)+delta(q), and active location mG(q). This is algebraically W-mW+mG: all centered residuals, candidate-wise spread, asymmetry, dependence and quantile spacings are preserved. The old warped coordinate mW, not active location mG, remains the sole ranking input to the unchanged K=3/M=40 stalled gate. Apply the same inherited sequential sampled-row maxima, without-replacement availability and ascending-pool-index exact ties to A inside that gate. The path of effect is a candidate-dependent location shift in function maxima, changed actual paid identities, real subsequent accepted fitting and breeding, then a conditional endpoint change. It introduces no refit, covariance change, draw, clipping, rescaling, blend coefficient, new acquisition rule or gate change. Predict complete correct execution and material actual set-membership exposure, followed by a macro gain of at least +0.002 versus the code Parent. Prospective proper loss, coverage and ordering remain separate diagnostics, and no causal mediation is claimed.

finding_summary.headline: Location translation meets the conditional endpoint target despite worse predictive loss and uneven task gains.
finding_summary.insights: This confirms a useful location substitution on this complete warped-law host, with the original gate held fixed. It does not show improved prediction: same-paid pinball loss worsened from 0.021294 for the unshifted law to 0.021481, ordering accuracy fell from 0.68944 to 0.68569, and 90% coverage fell from 70.44% to 69.82%. Full positive gain over actual generating parents also fell, from 15.60275 to 14.04774, while late-half gain rose slightly from 3.41489 to 3.45342 and late incumbent progress rose from 0.60829 to 0.86080. Prediction quality, local parent improvement and endpoint progress therefore remain distinct measurements; none is established as the causal mediator. The molecular audit shows smaller typical size and fewer large molecules, yet extreme expansion persists. Many graph identities still concentrate into a few leading ring families, and no atom stereochemistry is specified despite 2,247 records with potential unassigned centres. A proposal method that deliberately explores core topology and preserves or varies stereochemical assignments could address those observed coverage limits; its score benefit is untested. The existing Parent predictive verdict remains valid, and retained-component contributions and broader population reliability remain open.
finding_summary.results: All 435 original fits and all 4,350 prospective three-law predictions completed. The old eligibility gate and centered warped draws passed the preservation audit. Translation changed 191 purchased sets and introduced 473 actually purchased identities; 447 reached the next fit and the remaining 26 were final-batch observations. The endpoint macro rose from 0.563160 to 0.577516, a gain of 0.014355 that exceeds the registered 0.002 threshold. All three seed macros rose, although seven task/seed cells fell and seven rose, with one tie. Sitagliptin supplied more than the net improvement; the other four task means declined. The trusted paired task-safety rule passed against both the code Parent and formal Anchor. The Child remains 0.029515 below the formal Anchor, and its different code Parent makes the literal formal goal criterion inapplicable.

molecular.overall_character: All five frozen tasks and all Search seeds 0, 1, 2 have complete accepted trajectories for this Child and code Parent n-2723e9d54276: 300 records per cell, comprising ten initial and 290 optimizer observations. Each node therefore contributes 4,350 optimizer records and 150 initials; all 9,000 structures parse with RDKit 2023.09.6. Six supplied summaries agree with those counts and the observed maxima. The original request separately states child_complete=true and paired_complete=true, matched seeds [0,1,2], no profile mismatches and no tasks without trajectories. No requested trajectory or summary is missing. This completeness concerns the chemical record and endpoint pairing; it is not a preservation or mechanism verdict. The Child optimizer population has rings in 4,276/4,350 records and aromatic atoms in 4,253/4,350. Substituted fused aza-aromatics, aryl amides, imine/carbonyl heterocycles, and ring-associated amines are demonstrated capabilities. Typical heavy-atom size is 28 (median), versus Parent 29. Counts above 40/50/60 heavy atoms are 116/40/13 versus 240/94/27, yet the maximum rises to 96 from 88; smaller central size does not eliminate extreme expansion. Seventy versus 81 records have at most five heavy atoms, and 524 versus 827 exceed molecular weight 500. All Child optimizer records have no charged atoms and no specified atom chiral tags; 2,247 contain a potential unassigned chiral centre, versus 2,066 Parent. Neither node specifies double-bond stereochemistry in these records. Neutral graph representations do not establish the absence of ionizable groups or their solution protonation states. N-halogen connectivity decreases from 960 Parent to 654 Child records, while O-halogen connectivity increases from 35 to 348; N-O single bonds occur in 330 versus 456. These explicit connectivity flags support structure-specific chemical scrutiny, not a blanket assertion of instability, impossibility or biological harm. The finite output panel shows many ring topologies alongside concentrated local families. Accepted syntax, ordinary median size and high recorded objective values do not demonstrate synthesis, binding, selectivity or developability. All structural counts below are derived from accepted trajectories, separately from the digest SMILES-string counters. Counts preserve record occurrences across independent seeds. Initial records are retained separately in every audit. Typed/generic Murcko counts exclude empty scaffolds. Similarity is the mean of all within-task record pairs after excluding molecules with fewer than ten heavy atoms, using binary radius-2 chiral 2048-bit Morgan Tanimoto, matching the archived Parent report convention; it is not the optimizer count kernel. The highest-30 subset is pooled within task over three seeds, ordered by existing score then seed/evaluation for ties; it is selected retrospectively and is not an independent replicate. Per-cell highest/lowest-30 and full-record descriptors remain in the audits. No new objective call, predictive model evaluation or chemical scoring function was used. method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
